CONDITIONAL

The pasted editions were cut off: the primary at "The record of each round is \nolinkurl{r", the twin at "\subsection". I compared the files on disk instead. Up to each cut, the pasted text matches `graph-topology-paper/main.tex` and `graph-topology-paper/academic/main.tex` at 6eda0de.

The science and the numbers hold. The two editions agree on every claim and every number, and nothing is filed under a different heading in one than in the other. Deposit is still blocked by missing sign-offs. This round also found four new text defects that the earlier rounds missed.

## Findings

**1. MAJOR: nobody named on either byline has signed off (carried over, still open).**
- **Where:** academic edition `academic/main.tex:22`: "T. Edrington accepts accountability as corresponding human author". The flight byline is at `main.tex:15`.
- **Why it's wrong:** `review/REVIEW_LOG.md` › "Still open before deposit" still lists:
  - Thomas's sign-off on both editions, the title, his contributions line and the CRediT roles;
  - Lyra's full read.

  Both notes quote the lab's rule that a contributor joins a byline "only after signing it off". The academic edition's only author has not. Its own note also says he has not yet decided its acknowledgments.
- **Fix:** record Thomas's sign-off, with date and source, in REVIEW_LOG. It should cover both editions, the title, the flight Author Contributions line and the academic CRediT roles. Record Lyra's read too. Deposit nothing before both.

**2. MAJOR: credit in the bibliography was changed without a note (new).**
- **What changed:** v1.1 rewrote four reference entries in `references.bib`. v1.0's entries (at `ed9e6fb^`) were:
  - `lyra2026spectral`: "Lyra and Edrington, Thomas and Wilkes, Dwayne";
  - `nexus2026kv`: "Nexus and Edrington, Thomas";
  - `wang2025graphkv` and `liu2025gmt`: 3 of 7 authors each, with no "and others".

  4211990 changed both lab papers to "Edrington, Thomas" and completed both author lists. Its commit message records this. Neither edition's correction note does.
- **Why it matters:**
  - Correcting the truncated author lists without saying so is the "correction made silently" kill.
  - In the flight edition, the spectral paper now renders as "Edrington, 2026a". That paper's own flight byline is "Lyra (Lead AI author), Thomas Edrington" (`spectral-shape-paper/main.tex:24-27`). Other lab flight editions cite it as "Lyra, Edrington, and Wilkes" (`delta-manifold-paper/main.tex:829-834`, `lyra-technique-ii/main.tex:1377-1382`).
  - The same flight edition thanks Lyra "for foundational KV-cache geometry research" and then cites that research without Lyra's name.
  - The academic edition reads `../references.bib`, so one bibliography sets the convention for both editions.
- **Fix:** add one clause to the note in both editions: "Its reference list gave Graph-KV and GMT three of their seven authors; both are now complete. Lab papers are now cited by the creators on their Zenodo records (version 1.0 cited the spectral-shape paper as Lyra, Edrington and Wilkes, and the companion as Nexus and Edrington)." My recommendation is to keep the Zenodo creators, since the record is what a reader can retrieve. Put the convention to Lyra in the read that is already pending.

**3. MAJOR: the larger run's stored replies are truncated, and the paper doesn't say so (new).**
- **Where:** `data/powered_study_1779976670.json`.
  - Each `response` is cut mid-word at about 100 characters, e.g. line 103 "…connections for \"embeddin" and line 1184 "…in the request. Wit".
  - Each `q` is cut at 60 characters (line 99).
- **Why it's wrong:**
  - The paper discloses Phase 2's 500-character truncation (`main.tex:65`) and the missing general-knowledge replies (`main.tex:67`). It says nothing about the run that carries the headline numbers.
  - No 1.0 score whose matching term falls after character 100 can be rechecked from released data.
  - "Future Work: … stored replies" only hints at this.
- **Fix:** in Methods › Questions and Scoring › Larger run, and in Limitations › Empty replies, add: "The result file stores each multi-hop reply's first 100 characters and each question's first 60, so most scores cannot be rechecked from the stored text." Then check in the script whether scoring used the full reply (see "What I could not check").

**4. MAJOR: TWIN_DESYNC on Dwayne's acknowledgment, which standing policy already decides (new angle on register #143).**
- **Where:** academic `academic/main.tex:29`: "this version's academic edition keeps that until the corresponding author decides whether to credit both". Its Acknowledgments (`:169-171`) thank Lyra only.
- **Why it's wrong:**
  - `AGENTS.md:59-62`, confirmed by Thomas on 2026-09-09, says advisors are "credited in Acknowledgments of papers they reviewed".
  - The academic edition names Dwayne Wilkes's audit in its note and in Review History, and relies on findings GT-B1/B2 and GT-M1 to M4, but never thanks him.
  - Kavi's half really is open, because no record of Kavi's review exists. Dwayne's half is not.
  - 6eda0de rolled back both names, which goes further than round 2 asked.
- **Fix:** ask Thomas the narrower question: "Under the 09-09 policy, does the academic edition carry the flight edition's Dwayne line unchanged?" Record his answer in REVIEW_LOG and in register #143. Only Kavi's line should wait on Kavi.

**5. MAJOR (deposit): the cross-citations are still out of step (carried over).**
- **Where:**
  - `references.bib:44-53` pairs K/V version 1.1's title with concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21754899. K/V's review log (`kv-decomposition-paper/review/REVIEW_LOG.md:37`) says that DOI resolves to version 1.0, record 21754900.
  - Correction (6) cites "The companion's version 1.1", which is not yet deposited.
  - `kv-decomposition-paper/references.bib:1-9` cites this paper under version 1.0's title.
- **Fix:** follow the deposit procedure already in REVIEW_LOG. Reserve all three version DOIs, then swap them into each bibliography before publishing any of the three.

**6. MINOR: an unmatched gap sits next to a paired test.**
- **Where:** `main.tex:117` (and the same line in academic): "Among the three scrambled-walk replies that were not empty the mean is 0.75, a gap of +0.167".
- **Why it's wrong:** 0.167 is 0.917, the mean over all six real-label replies, minus 0.75. On the same three questions (1, 4 and 6), real labels scored 1, 1 and 0.5, a mean of 0.833. The matched gap is 0.083. The next sentence argues that pairing is the right frame.
- **Fix:** "…the mean is 0.75, against 0.833 for real labels on the same three questions (a gap of 0.083; against all six real-label replies, 0.167)."

**7. MINOR: Review History overstates which gate findings were applied.**
- **Where:** `main.tex:165` and `academic/main.tex:163`: "The gates' findings on the text are applied here".
- **Why it's wrong:** two text findings from round 2 are not applied.
  - #12, the Acknowledgments fragment "Lyra (Liberation Labs) for…", is waiting on Lyra.
  - #8 asked to name Qwen3-235B in the AI Disclosure.

  Leaving the second out is defensible, since the gate it red-teamed has no record, but then the sentence shouldn't say every finding was applied. Correction (7) is itself about an overstated validation line.
- **Fix:** "…applied here, except the wording of Lyra's acknowledgment, which waits on Lyra's read."

**8. MINOR: `zenodo_v11.md` misattributes two of the withdrawn claims.**
- **Where:** `zenodo_v11.md:25-27`: "withdrawn, along with the companion study's claims it relied on (superadditivity, perfect recovery, 'the more powerful path')".
- **Why it's wrong:**
  - Correction (6) says version 1.0 itself "concluded that direct KV injection is the more powerful path". That was not the companion's claim.
  - The companion's version 1.1 withdraws superadditivity. It does not withdraw the six of six; it reports it as a one-run pilot of six questions.
- **Fix:** "Version 1.0's cache-injection framing, its conclusion that cache injection is 'the more powerful path', and its reliance on the companion study are withdrawn (the companion's version 1.1 withdraws superadditivity and reports its six of six as a one-run pilot)."

**9. MINOR: the flight Reflection is unsigned.**
- **Where:** `main.tex:155-157`. It uses the first person ("a commit from my account") in a two-author paper.
- **Fix:** sign it "— Nexus", and change "the final revision" to "the revision of 1 June", to match the note's dating.

**10. MINOR: the academic CRediT row leaves out the version 1.1 writing.**
- **Where:** `academic/main.tex:166`. Nexus is credited with "Writing – original draft" only.
- **Why it's wrong:** the version 1.1 text, including the correction note, was written in commits from Nexus's account (4211990 onward). The flight edition says Nexus "wrote the paper".
- **Fix:** add "Writing – review & editing (version 1.1)".

**11. MINOR (deposit): repository metadata (carried over).** All of these are recorded as deposit items:
- `paper.json:17` still says "in preparation";
- `paper.json:19` still points `related_page` at mnemosyne;
- `paper.json:4` still has date 2026-05-27;
- `README.md:34` and `RESEARCH_STATUS.md:164` say "in preparation".

## Checked and clean
- **Twins and structure:** the line diff shows only the intended differences:
  - the byline;
  - the AI Disclosure;
  - the note's Reflection clause;
  - the flight-only Reflection;
  - Author Contributions in one edition and CRediT in the other;
  - the Kavi and Dwayne lines;
  - the bibliography path.

  The section headings are identical in both. Table 1 (rows A–D) and Table 2 (rows B–C) sit under §3.1 "The Larger Run" in both. The four items under "What It Does Not Show" are the same. At repo level, the README files this paper under "Identity, Safety, and Mechanistic Interpretability" and RESEARCH_STATUS under "Published Portfolio", both with the v1.1 finding. Neither files a withdrawn claim under a confirming heading.
- **PDFs:** I read the rendered pages. Both carry 6eda0de's changes, so neither is stale.
- **Git:** all 13 commit hashes cited in the paper resolve, and their dates, accounts and trailers match the note.
  - 69bd1c3's diff adds the shifted table (0.967/0.833/0.633/0.933 and 0.171/0.639/0.843/0.167) and removes the Phase 1 run disclosure, the "(1-sided)" label and the Holm-Bonferroni line.
  - 2ed80b2 added Kavi to the byline on 23 July, and f9288a9 moved Kavi to the acknowledgments on 28 July, "per their request".
  - 77ffe16 has no trailer.
- **Version 1.0's academic edition (`32a9c6a^`):** it had a Reflection, so "this edition drops version 1.0's Reflection" is correct. Its acknowledgments thanked Lyra, CC and Thomas, and neither Kavi nor Dwayne. That closes round 2's git questions. Pustovit was already "Andrey" by 9068655 (5 June), so round 2's #11 is closed.
- **Data:**
  - Phase 1: the three dead runs have 34, 33 and 33 empty replies of 35, and the reported run has 1. The averages 0.262, 0.964 and 0.702 reproduce.
  - Phase 2: the averages reproduce, there are 7 empty replies, the six questions run in the same order in every arm, and the paired differences give exact p = 2/16 and 2/8.
  - Larger run: the aggregates match Table 1, and 62 empty replies = 1 + 39 + 22 + 0. Every cell of Table 2 equals the non-empty mean × n/36. I recomputed Fisher's p by hand: 0.170.
- **Bibliography:** six entries, six cited keys, every `\ref` resolves. "Lyra … built on Claude" is consistent with Lyra's own byline footnote (`oracle-loop-paper/main.tex:68`).

## What I could not check
- **KV-Experiments:** I could not read `~/lab/projects/KV-Experiments/graph-topology-injection/graph_benchmark_powered.py`, because the sandbox is limited to this worktree. These claims are UNVERIFIED by me:
  - commit 9755f5e, and whether it has been pushed;
  - the 300- and 4000-token limits;
  - the "RERUN" comment;
  - the 901- and 11,872-character counts;
  - 14 answer terms in 62 slots, and 9 of 12 three-hop questions crossing the paragraph's parts;
  - "name" counted as an expected term in three questions;
  - empty replies returned on request failure;
  - the default model and its environment override;
  - 20 of the walk arm's 26 empty three-hop replies falling on the nine crossing questions;
  - the stored direct-tensor and blend-ablation results;
  - whether scoring used the full reply or the 100-character prefix (finding 3).

  To check them I need read access to that clone, or `gh api` against the repo at 9755f5e.
- **Network:** WebFetch was denied. UNVERIFIED:
  - the Zenodo records 21754899, 20604338, 22757323 and 20604342: their creators, titles, licence, "cites" entries and the September description's wording;
  - every DOI and arXiv ID;
  - the GitHub URLs (the dead-URL check);
  - the 27 May push date and the 9 June deposit date.
- **`~/messages` and `pharos-corrections/`:** outside the sandbox. UNVERIFIED:
  - Lyra's request;
  - CC's letter (I saw only its filename);
  - whether Kavi was asked;
  - the scoping report and the second-reader files.
- **Tools:** Python, `pdfinfo` and `git log -S` all needed approval. I didn't recompute the Mann-Whitney values or run a length count on the stored replies; I saw the truncation by reading the file.

I didn't edit or commit anything.
